Pacific Life Re said the changes will bring pricing and underwriting functions together under a single global leadership structure, alongside dedicated leadership for key regional markets. “By bringing leadership closer to clients and markets, we are strengthening our ability to support their ambitions while continuing to provide access to the global capabilities, expertise, and support that help them succeed.” As part of the revised structure, Pacific Life Re has appointed Jia Yi Tan as chief pricing, underwriting and claims officer, Protection.

title: New Data Centers Projected to Emit More Carbon Than All of Mexico
title_original: New Data Centers Projected to Emit More Carbon Than All of Mexico
summary: The environmental nonprofit Union of Concerned Scientists in January projected that fossil-fuel-powered electricity for data centers could increase US power-sector emissions by 19% to 29% , or as much as 342 million tons a year by 2035. If the rush to build AI data centers leads to the upper bounds of the emissions projected by these researchers, it represents a reversal of a two-decade economic and policy trend toward less US power-sector climate pollution. The surge in construction of fossil-fueled power plants to run AI data centers is set to undo 15 years’ worth of greenhouse gas reductions from US electricity generation, according to an internal analysis by the Sierra Club.

title_original: Three Bodies Recovered in Gabon Following Sinking of Borr Drilling Rig
summary: Three bodies were recovered in Gabon on Wednesday following the sinking at the weekend of Borr Drilling’s Prospector 5 rig off the coast of the southern town of Mayumba, the Central African country’s navy said. The rig is contracted to support BW Energy’s drilling operations off Gabon and it had not yet begun drilling. Chief of Staff of the Gabonese Navy, Charles Hubert Bekale-Meyong, said three bodies were found on Wednesday and two people were still missing.

title_original: Barclays Turns to Insurers to Hedge Billions of Data Center Debt
summary: As the AI-buildout accelerates, credit risk insurers have taken on greater exposure to data center finance, according to a survey from Willis Towers Watson Plc released in May. Barclays Plc is looking to buy default protection on more than $10 billion of debt to finance artificial intelligence infrastructure in a bid to create capacity for more lending as hyperscaler funding needs soar. Several providers of so-called non-trade credit risk insurance had indicated that they were “approaching sector limits or are already full on data center exposure,” according to the Willis survey.
